list.title: Automations
list.emptyBody: Set one up yourself — a morning inbox summary, a reply draft for every customer email, a watch on competitor pricing.

describe.title: Describe what to automate
describe.placeholder: When a new email with an invoice arrives, save the PDF to Drive and log it in my sheet

examples.weeklyReport: Every Monday at 9:00, collect last week's numbers and write a report
examples.inbox: Every weekday, start sometime between 8:00 and 9:30 and work through my inbox
examples.customerEmail: When I get an email from a customer, draft a reply
examples.competitorPricing: When competitor pricing changes, compare it with ours and update the battlecard

events.emptyBody: When an automation starts, is skipped or fails, it shows up here.
events.unavailableBody: Update Godmode on your computer to see every automation's events here.

automation.title: Automation
automation.deleteMessageApp: Godmode stops listening for “{{trigger}}” in {{app}}. Past runs and conversations stay in your history.
automation.deleteMessageWebhook: Its webhook URL stops working. Past runs and conversations stay in your history.
automation.deleteMessage: It won't run again. Past runs and conversations stay in your history.
automation.openRunChat: Opens the chat of this run
automation.changeTriggerOnComputer: Change the trigger in Godmode on your computer.
automation.enabledHint: Paused automations keep their settings but don't run.
automation.enabledHintEvents: Paused automations keep their settings and ignore new events.
automation.loginsFillOnly: Filled in, raw passwords stay hidden

empty.scheduleBody: Runs show up here when the schedule fires.
empty.conditionBody: Once a check finds the condition true, it shows up here.
empty.webhookBody: Call the webhook URL — or send a test event — and it shows up here.

reveal.title: Reveal secrets to AI
reveal.footer: An agent set this automation up, so its runs fill logins into pages but can't read passwords or 2FA codes. Switch on only if you trust the prompt above.

runOn.label: Run on
runOn.anyHint: Runs where your schedules run: the primary, or another computer while it stands in.
runOn.pickedHint: Only {{name}} runs it, also while another computer stands in. A time it misses while away runs when it's back.
runOn.pickedOfflineHint: Only {{name}} runs it, also while another computer stands in. A time it misses while away runs when it's back (it's offline now).
runOn.unlistedHint: Pinned to a computer that isn't listed: one that left the group (the primary runs it then), or one this computer can't see while the primary is away.

edit.intro: When it happens, the agent gets to work — even while you're away.
edit.conditionPlaceholder: a competitor changes the price of their Pro plan (acme.com/pricing)
edit.conditionHint: In plain language. The agent checks it on the schedule below and gets to work once it's true.
edit.filterHint: In plain language. Events that don't match are skipped; leave empty to act on every event.
edit.keepOneChat: Every run continues the same chat, so it remembers previous runs.
edit.keepOneChatEvent: Every event continues the same chat. Off: each event gets its own chat, named after it.

problem.name: Name your automation
problem.prompt: Tell the agent what to do each time
problem.promptEvent: Tell the agent what to do with each event
problem.moreApps: Finish or remove the other app events

promptPlaceholder.schedule: Collect last week's numbers from Stripe and Google Analytics, write a short report and send it to me.
promptPlaceholder.app: Save the invoice PDF to Drive and log sender, amount and due date in my Invoices sheet. The event details are passed along.
promptPlaceholder.condition: Compare their new plans with ours and update the pricing battlecard in Notion. What the check found is passed along.
promptPlaceholder.webhook: Check whether the order qualifies for a recovery offer and draft a friendly email. The request body is passed along.

filterPlaceholder.app: the sender is a customer, or the subject mentions an invoice

triggerHint.schedule: Every morning, each Monday, on the 1st…
triggerHint.app: A new email, Slack message, calendar event…
triggerHint.webhook: Any service that can send an HTTP POST

notifyFooter.never: No notifications. A failing automation still shows under Needs you. Set up or changed on the phone, its runs fill in logins but never read raw passwords.
notifyFooter.always: A notification after every run, with what it did. Set up or changed on the phone, its runs fill in logins but never read raw passwords.
notifyFooter.failures: A failure is told once, until a run works again. Set up or changed on the phone, its runs fill in logins but never read raw passwords.

edit.checkModelHint: A smaller, faster model keeps frequent checks cheap; the work itself uses the agent's model.
edit.webhookAfterSave: You'll get the URL right after saving.
edit.webhookAfterCreate: You'll get the URL right after creating it.

notifyFooterFull.never: No notifications. A failing automation still shows under Needs you.
notifyFooterFull.always: A notification after every run, with what it did.
notifyFooterFull.failures: A failure is told once, until a run works again.

appTrigger.pickEvent: Pick the event to react to
appTrigger.connectFirstDescription: App events come from Composio. Add your Composio API key and connect Gmail, Slack, Calendar or any other app — then pick what should start this automation.
appTrigger.chooseAgentFirst: Choose the agent first — it can only watch accounts it has access to.
appTrigger.noUsableDescription: The connected accounts belong to other agents or workspaces. Connect one for {{name}}, its workspace or globally, then pick the event that starts this automation.
appTrigger.noAppsDescription: Connect an app like Gmail, Slack or Google Calendar on the Integrations page, then come back to pick the event that starts this automation.
appTrigger.pollHint: Composio checks {{app}} for this every few minutes, so new events can take a few minutes to arrive.
appTrigger.needsSetup: Needs a one-time setup in {{app}} before events arrive.
appTrigger.noEvents: {{app}} doesn't offer any events to react to. Try a condition instead — the agent checks it regularly.

testEvent.invalidJson: That looks like JSON but doesn't parse. Fix it, or send plain text.
testEvent.descriptionApp: Runs “{{name}}” as if {{app}} sent this. The filter is checked just as for a real event.
testEvent.descriptionWebhook: Runs “{{name}}” as if its URL was called with this. The filter is checked just as for a real event.
testEvent.title: Send a test event
testEvent.hint: JSON or plain text. Leave it empty to send a small example.

webhook.locked: Unlock the vault to see the URL.
webhook.lockedHint: The secret part is stored encrypted.
webhook.warning: Anyone with this URL can start the automation. Rotate it if it leaks.
webhook.rotateDescription: Godmode issues a new secret URL. Anything still calling the old one gets an error until you update it.
webhook.rotatedDescription: The old URL no longer works — update the services that call it.
webhook.title: Webhook URL
webhook.localOnly: This address only works on the computer itself. To receive calls from other services, reach Godmode through a tunnel or reverse proxy and use the same path.
